title: Sandboxed approval UX and log retention experiments
body:
Background and intent:

This is a working sketch: explore a low-friction, sandboxed approval UX for customer-managed networks (VPC/on-prem) paired with compact audit log retention experiments. The goal is to reduce customer onboarding friction while preserving sufficient forensic evidence for post-incident analysis and compliance requests. This doc collects hypotheses, UX drafts, proposed retention buckets, telemetry, and a lightweight evidence exchange format to prototype in the next pilot cohort.

Problem statement:
- Private deployments require explicit change approvals for inbound/outbound connectors, egress rules, and operator-delegated changes.
- Current flows are heavy: full immutable audit bundles + long retention by default -> onboarding slowness and operations overhead for small customers.
- Customers want control over log residency and cost; security/compliance teams want demonstrable provenance and short incident debug time.

Primary goals (measurable):
1) Reduce average time-to-first-successful-VPC-handoff from 5d -> 1d for SMB pilots.
2) Maintain >= 90% of postmortem-relevant evidence in a compact form (sufficient to reconstruct causally-important change sequence) for 30d.
3) Keep production overhead (bytes stored per approval) < 10KB on average for sandboxed approvals.

Non-goals:
- This is not replacing enterprise immutable-archive features (full evidence retention for regulated customers).
- Not tackling KMS/escrow policy changes here — assume existing KMS integrations for signing.

Key concepts / vocabulary (informal):
- sandboxed-approval: a temporary, lightweight approval flow used during onboarding and low-risk operator tasks. Evidence is bounded and sampled.
- evidence-shard: a compact, signed summary of an approval (metadata + diffs + small artifacts) intended for short-term retention.
- proof-snapshot: a richer bundle reserved for full-attestation customers or escalations.

Proposed flow (UX sketch):
1) Customer initiates VPC handoff via Console -> selects "Sandboxed onboarding" (opt-in checkbox) with explicit TTL (30d default).
2) System shows minimal required approvals (e.g., allowlist IP, route, egress policy) with suggested operator signers.
3) Operator approves in-console or via CLI; lightweight evidence-shard is created and stored in short retention bucket.
4) For any security-sensitive change, the system escalates to full proof-snapshot generation automatically (policy triggers e.g., port open > 1024, public egress).

Evidence types and retention buckets (experiments):
- ephemeral-shard (default): 30d retention, compressed JSON summary (~3-8KB), base64-encoded signature, sample telemetry hashes.
- audit-slim (optional): 90d retention, includes patch-diff and operator annotation (~12-20KB).
- full-proof (enterprise): 7y parity with existing enterprise retention, includes full logs, binary artifacts, signed snapshots.

Minimal evidence-shard schema (plain-text example):
- shard_id: uuid
- change_type: egress-rule / route-add / connector-auth
- actor: operator@customer.example.com (or redwood-operator)
- timestamp: ISO8601
- summary: one-line human-friendly summary
- diff_hash: sha256(hex) of the patch (not the full patch)
- sample_log_refs: [short hashes] (pointers to telemetry slices stored elsewhere)
- signature: base64(sig)
- ttl_expires: ISO8601

Note: the actual implementation should avoid embedding large patches; the shard intentionally stores a diff_hash + pointers to sampled logs.

Decision heuristics for auto-escalation (examples):
- Any rule that opens a public 0.0.0.0/0 TCP port -> full-proof required.
- New outbound connector to third-party SaaS with sensitive scopes -> full-proof.
- Otherwise, sandboxed with audit-slim sampling rate 1/10 for first 72 hours.

Telemetry and observability (what we need to measure during the pilot):
- time_to_approval: seconds from request creation to last signer.
- shard_byte_size: distribution, median + 95th percentile.
- shard_lookup_success: whether shard resolves to sufficient logs when requested.
- escalation_rate: percent of sandboxed approvals that escalate to full-proof.
- postmortem_sufficiency_score: manual scoring for a sample of incidents (0..5).

Console UX micro-interactions (draft):
- Inline toggle: [ Sandbox onboarding ] (tooltip: "Shorter retention, fewer artifacts — good for pilots; can be escalated anytime")
- TTL preset buttons: 7d / 30d / 90d / enterprise
- Evidence preview: small modal showing shard fields, signature, and a link to request the full-proof ("Request escalation")
- Audit export: allow operators to export zipped shards for local archive (signed; export count tracked).

Customer-managed networking handshake (minimal):
- During the handoff, customer provides an operator public-key bundle + desired retention policy.
- Redwood system generates a handoff packet: {shard pointer, required signers, suggested TTL} signed by Redwood control-plane key.
- Customer-side agent (or SRE) uses the handoff packet to apply changes; operator signatures returned to Redwood.
- Agent receipts are optional for sandboxed flow to reduce friction; required for full-proof path.

Risk analysis and mitigations (quick):
- Risk: Loss of forensic detail -> mitigation: keep sampled logs and provide ability to escalate retrospective full-proof capture within a short window (48h).
- Risk: Customer misunderstands sandbox and assumes compliance parity -> mitigation: clear UI copy + mandatory checkbox + onboarding email + audit trail showing retention TTL.
- Risk: Signatures can be replayed -> mitigation: shard_id nonce + timestamp + TTL + signature scheme with replay protection.

Operational considerations / infra notes (rough):
- Storage tiers: cheap short-term blob store (for shards), mid-term index with pointers, long-term archive for full-proof (S3 Glacier style).
- Indexing: shards must be queryable by shard_id, actor, customer_id, and change_type.
- Cost: estimate 10KB * N_shards_per_month per customer (pilot target N=200) => ~2MB/customer/month raw.
- Sampling: telemetry slices used for evidence must be retained for at least 7d beyond shard TTL to support escalations.

Acceptance criteria for pilot (MVP):
- Console: sandbox toggle + TTL presets implemented and persisted in handoff flow.
- Backend: shard generation pipeline and short-term storage (30d) + basic index API.
- Telemetry: time_to_approval + shard_byte_size + escalation_rate dashboards in Redwood Console.
- Security: shard signatures verified server-side; replay nonce enforced.

Open questions / TODOs (prioritized):
- Q1: exact shard schema: do we include a small redaction-friendly patch (200-500 bytes) vs. only hashes? (owner: Evan)
- Q2: how easy is it to trigger retrospective full-proof capture? cost/feasibility? (owner: Lina)
- Q3: legal/compliance language: what disclosures are required for opting into short retention? (owner: Mateo)
- Q4: should we allow customer-managed storage endpoints (S3) for shards in sandbox? (risk: customer deletes early) (owner: Priya)
- Q5: sample size and default sampling rate for audit-slim -> propose 1/10 first 72h, then 1/100.

Pilot plan (timeline rough):
- Week 0-2: finalize shard schema + escalation heuristics + signs API prototype.
- Week 3-5: Console toggle + TTL UI + backend shard pipeline + index.
- Week 6-8: Run 3-customer pilot (SMB and 1 mid-market) -> collect telemetry + manual postmortem scoring.
- Week 9: review and decide next steps (wider rollout vs revert to enterprise-only).

Notes / quick references:
- Related: PRIV-approval-sim-harness (linked JIRA) for testing sampling heuristics.
- Quick prototype repo: github.com/redwood-inference/approval-protos — PR #117 has early shard spec.

Rough draft copy for console tooltip and checkbox (copywriter help required):
"Sandboxed onboarding: Generate a compact, signed summary of network changes retained for a short period. Good for pilot and low-risk changes. This is not a substitute for long-term compliance archives. You can request a full forensic bundle at any time; escalation may have additional costs and delays"

Next immediate actions (this week):
- Evan: propose final shard JSON YAML and sample payloads (due 2024-10-07).
- Lina: feasibility spike on retrospective capture and storage costs (2024-10-09).
- Mateo: draft compliance blurb for UI + email template (2024-10-11).
- Priya: schedule sync with infra + security to validate signature scheme and replay protection (2024-10-04).

Appendix: small experiment notes (raw):
- Tried compacting actual approval artifacts from past 8 customers: median 14KB, mean 48KB (outliers where full binary blobs included). If we strip patches and store only hashes + pointers, median drops to ~4.2KB.
- Escalation rate observed historically for similar relaxed flows: ~6-12% in first 72h.

This doc is intentionally rough. Goal: land a small pilot by end of Q4 and learn whether sandboxed approvals materially speed onboarding without unacceptable forensic tradeoffs.
